prompt: Implement ImageFlip.flipHorizontal and ImageFlip.flipVertical. Each returns a new mirrored image and leaves the source unchanged.
explanation: A mirror is a pure index transformation: reading the source at (width - 1 - x, y) while writing the output at (x, y) reverses each row, and reading at (x, height - 1 - y) reverses the column order. Because the pixels themselves are unchanged you can move whole packed ints with getRGB and setRGB instead of unpacking channels. Writing into a new BufferedImage rather than the source is what makes flipping twice give the original image back.
hints: The output pixel you are filling in and the source pixel you read from have different coordinates -- work out the source index from x, y and the image size.
For a horizontal mirror, x = 0 must pull from the last column, and the last column index is width - 1.
You do not need to split the colour into red, green and blue: out.setRGB(x, y, src.getRGB(...)) moves the whole pixel.
